Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

3. Material— According to Indian Standard Specification for shuttle blocks 



4. Shuttle Arcessories — Various accessories used In making shuttle shall preferably conform to the 
relevant requirements laid down In IS 6266-1971 ' Specification for accessories far use In shuttles for plain

J. Weight — The weight of a shuttle shall be as agreed to between the buyer and the seller subject to a 
tolerance of ±5 percent 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The wood for the manufacture of shuttles shall be fully-seasoned ( see*IS : I Ml- I9S8 Code of practice 
for seasoning of timber ( tentative)] 



4.3 The outer surface and surfaces where the yarn comes In conact shall be finished smooth 

1.4 Angle of shuttle ( bevel ) shall be between 84 to 87* subject to • tolerance of ± 0-8* on ths angle 
prescribed by the buyer

A 5 If agreed to between the buyer and the seller, shuttles made of uncompressed wood shall be 
Impregnated with raw linseed oil 

7. Balancing of Shuttle— When the shuttle Is held between two horizontal frlctlonless bearings (or 
thumb nails) so that the shuttle front faces the viewer the shuttle shall tilt towards the back 

I. Dropping Test — When the shuttle Is vertically dropped with one of Its tips facing down from a height 
of one metre on a cast Iron plate the tip shall not get blunt 

9. Position of Pirn— The pirn, when In position In a shuttle, shsll lie at equidistance from Inside 
opposite walla of the shuttle However, the difference In gap on either aide shall not exceed 1 mm. 

10. Marking— Mark each shuttle at a suitable place with the following 

a) Brand or trade-mark of the manufacturer, 

b) Hand of the shuttle whether right hand ( R) cr left hand ( L), and 

c) Code number to trace back history of production 

14.1 Certification Marking — Details available with the Bureau of Indian Standards
